corrections.before:
The conditional partial-health estimate is about $10.5 million per 10 MSA QALYs. This is not the complete portfolio return or a lower bound.

The central resource bridge allocates 50% of annual recipient capacity to community overdose prevention and assumes $1,000 per unique risk-person year: approximately 1063 people. Neither number is a verified service allocation or actual annual reach. They are explicit planning priors given the absence of recipient-level outcome data. The encounter rate is 0.1 per person-year, additional timely rescue is 30%, and avoided mortality hazard per incremental encounter is 0.1. This yields a 0.003 annual hazard reduction for one year, before the 25% ordinary-gift response.

Baseline mortality is 8% annually and utility 0.7, both judgments. After the first year, both groups face the same mortality hazard; any survival difference is followed for at most ten years with 3% discounting. Repeat overdose is therefore not awarded another lifetime. A 65% MSA share applies only to the modeled beneficiaries and is deliberately uncertain, with 40% and 80% alternatives. No full New Jersey or CSA denominator is substituted.

Wide positive alternatives vary delivery efficiency, rescue opportunity, substitution, funding and duration. Zero and net harm remain possible. A 25% added-resource case changes cost only, testing omitted partner and volunteer inputs without pretending those resources produce more beneficiaries.

The conditional partial-health estimate is about $10.5 million per 10 MSA QALYs. This is not the complete portfolio return or a lower bound.

The central resource bridge allocates 50% of annual recipient capacity to community overdose prevention and assumes $1,000 per unique risk-person year: approximately 1063 people. Neither number is a verified service allocation or actual annual reach. They are explicit planning priors given the absence of recipient-level outcome data. The encounter rate is 0.1 per person-year, additional timely rescue is 30%, and avoided mortality hazard per incremental encounter is 0.1. This yields a 0.003 annual hazard reduction for one year, before the 25% ordinary-gift response.

Baseline mortality hazard is 0.08 per year (about 7.69% annual death risk), and utility is 0.7; both are judgments. After the first year, both groups face the same mortality hazard; any survival difference is followed for at most ten years with 3% discounting. Repeat overdose is therefore not awarded another lifetime. A 65% MSA share applies only to the modeled beneficiaries and is deliberately uncertain, with 40% and 80% alternatives. No full New Jersey or CSA denominator is substituted.

Wide positive alternatives vary delivery efficiency, rescue opportunity, substitution, funding and duration. Zero and net harm remain possible. A 25% added-resource case changes cost only, testing omitted partner and volunteer inputs without pretending those resources produce more beneficiaries.
corrections.reason: Hazard is not identical to annual mortality probability.

corrections.before: U=C*f/k; delta=e*t*l; dlog=ln(1+d); F(v,t)=(1-exp(-v*t))/v; H=U*u*[F(m-delta+dlog,1)-F(m+dlog,1)+(exp(-(m-delta))-exp(-m))*exp(-dlog)*F(m+dlog,T-1)]; Qall=b*H-h; QMSA=g*Qall. Cost sensitivities change numerator only.
corrections.after: U=C*f/k; delta=e*t*l; dlog=ln(1+d); F(v,t)=(1-exp(-v*t))/v; H=U*u*[F(m-delta+dlog,1)-F(m+dlog,1)+(exp(-(m-delta))-exp(-m))*exp(-dlog)*F(m+dlog,T-1)]; Qall=b*H-h; QMSA=g*Qall. Cost sensitivities change numerator only. The encounter-level mortality input l is mapped linearly into a hazard decrement delta=e*t*l as an approximation, not an exact probability-to-hazard identity.

corrections.before: The organization describes work on cooling access and implementation. The Council's enacted law requires covered rental sleeping rooms to have qualifying cooling by June 2030, subject to tenant elections and other conditions. Rules, affordability, uptake and enforcement therefore matter more than the existence of the law. Request a campaign-specific baseline, additional households able to use cooling, tenant costs, agency commitments and evidence of NYC-EJA's contribution. [Original law](https://legistar.council.nyc.gov/LegislationDetail.aspx?GUID=156F95BB-CA74-44F3-A07B-A0E54EA0C10F&ID=6788510)

corrections.after: Whole annual expense / 85 historical screened people = $101,293.85 per screened person, a portfolio accounting ratio. Central effective additional care equivalents = 85*0.25*0.5*0.5 = 5.3125 before the 85% residency allocation; full expense / local equivalent = about $1.91 million. These are judgment-based additional-care units, not documented clinical successes.
corrections.reason: Add interpretable native accounting and causal unit.

corrections.after: Central donor-attributable deaths avoided are 500*0.01*0.25*0.2*0.5 = 0.125 per annual cohort and 0.625 over five cohorts, before timing discount. Three-year recipient cost / 0.625 = $12,020,236.80 per conditional death avoided; finite competing-risk survival then determines QALYs. No deaths are claimed as observed campaign outcomes.
corrections.reason: Expose native outcomes before finite survival.

corrections.after: Central assumed U = 2,125,515*0.5/1000 = 1,062.7575 unique risk-person years. Whole-recipient expense / assumed risk-person year is $2,000, not the branch allocation cost of $1,000. Additional timely-rescue equivalents = U*0.1*0.3*0.25 = 7.97068125 before residency, giving $410,256.41 per modeled MSA rescue equivalent. A rescue is not a death averted; finite unique-person survival is calculated separately.
corrections.reason: Separate full-gift cost, allocation cost and additional rescue units.
